intelligence.human_view: 200% is not 20% with enthusiasm — it is a different number, and the number was the instruction. When he says 20%, the page must be 20% bigger than the original, and the original is the too-small version the instruction was measured against — not the current oversized one, not a guess. A remade copy is never the real thing: the Dashboard digit tiles already exist, already look real, already are the standard — harvest them verbatim and the numbers are real by construction, because they ARE the real numbers. And the placement is the elegance: middle, black area, perfect spacing all round, lined up — classy and clean and nice. Too small was wrong, too big is wrong, 20% is the number — the middle is the answer, and the middle is measurable: 20% is a number, not a feeling.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine someone asks you to make your drawing just a tiny bit bigger — a little bit, like this much — and instead you make it HUGE, ten times bigger, so it doesn't even fit on the paper! That's silly. Shawn asked for just a little bit bigger — 20%, not 200%. And the numbers should be the REAL numbers from the Dashboard, not copies someone drew again — because copies always look a little bit weird.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, Shawn says the calendar numbers are far too big, dear — he asked for 20% bigger, not 200% bigger, just a little bit, so only the number fits in its box. And they aren't even the real numbers, dear — they're copies someone remade, and copies always look a little bit odd. The real ones are right there on the Dashboard, dear — take those, exactly 20% bigger than the little ones, sitting right in the middle of the black, beautifully lined up. Classy and clean and nice, dear — that's the bar.
